title: Venice Tops List of World's Quietest Cities
paragraphs: Going on vacation to a big city doesn't have to mean living with noise. In fact, many cities can be very quiet.
Try Venice, Italy, for example, which has been named the world's quietest city on a list shared by Avanti Travel Insurance.

The company started by looking at Euromonitor's 2025 list of the 100 best city destinations. It then measured a 2-kilometre radius from the center of each city and looked at how many big, noisy roads were in this area, and how long they were.

It also looked at how many of the streets in the area were for pedestrians only, and finalized the top 10 by seeing if they had rules that could make an area more peaceful, like limits on store opening times and on traffic at nearby airports.
Venice's famous canals helped push it to the top of the list: instead of cars and buses, people get around the city center by boat or on foot.

Many stores in Venice also close on Sundays, with some not opening on Monday mornings either. It's also normal for food stores to close on Wednesday afternoons, giving the city center's already pedestrianized streets some very quiet hours.
Italy had two more cities in the top 10 after Venice, with Milan at number eight and Florence at number nine. Every city in the top 10 was in Europe.

The second quietest city on the list was Lisbon, Portugal, which has few busy roads in its center and a limit on the number of night flights at its main airport. This means a quiet night is less likely to be interrupted by a Boeing 737 flying overhead!
The third quietest city was Amsterdam in the Netherlands. Like Venice, canals and car-free streets keep things quiet in this popular tourist destination.
